finding.claim: Stored SSRF (MEDIUM, blind): the user-supplied `icon` URL is stored without any validation and fetched by the nightly job. The scheme, host and port are all attacker-controlled, so the server can be made to request internal or cloud-metadata addresses. The response body is discarded into a byte array that is never returned to the user, so this is blind SSRF (port scanning, internal probing, timing inference). Redirect following depends on the injected HttpClient, which is not configured in this repo; the Java default is Redirect.NEVER.
finding.source: `icon` parameter of PUT /profile, Profile.update(String webhook, String icon) at src/Profile.java:11. It is assigned to this.iconUrl at line 16 with no validation.
finding.sink: HttpClient.send(HttpRequest.newBuilder().uri(URI.create(iconUrl)).GET().build(), ...) at src/Profile.java:23-24, run by the nightly sync() job.

trace.note: this.iconUrl = icon, stored with no scheme or host check (only `webhook` is validated, at line 12)
nightly sync(HttpClient c) reads the stored value later (Check 4, stored URL fetched later)
URI.create(iconUrl) is passed to HttpRequest and c.send(...) issues a GET to the attacker-chosen host

finding.guards_checked: No validation of iconUrl anywhere on the path, either at storage (line 16) or at fetch time (line 23). The regex at line 12 covers only `webhook`. The authorization on PUT /profile is not visible in this repo; the skill rates authenticated endpoints MEDIUM rather than closing them. Redirect handling is not set here (HttpClient is injected), and the Java default is Redirect.NEVER. Severity is MEDIUM because the response is discarded (blind). The skill rates a stored two-hop URL HIGH if both steps are low-privilege, so it would be HIGH if the response were exposed.

verdict.reason: src/Profile.java:16 stores `icon` unvalidated (the regex at line 12 covers only `webhook`) and src/Profile.java:23 fetches it via URI.create(iconUrl) with no scheme or host check, so it is a blind SSRF; the endpoint's auth isn't visible in the repo, and the response is discarded into a byte array (line 24).
